newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deficit cuts without austerity - govt spokesman.
newsitem.headline: French deficit cuts without austerity - govt spokesman.

text.p: France's Socialist-led government aims to reduce public deficits "without an austerity plan" to qualify for a single European currency, government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said on Thursday.

"Our goal is indeed to reduce public deficits, irrespective of the euro, because we currently have a very high level of indebtedness", she said in a briefing to reporters following a morning cabinet meeting.

"(Our aim) is obviously to be able to come close, by reducing public deficits, to conditions laid out (in the Maastricht treaty), but to do so without an austerity plan and under conditions suitable for implementing our political plans," she said.
She declined to comment on a report in financial daily La Tribune which said the audit would show a public deficit of 3.6 to 3.7 percent of GDP in 1997 without corrective action.
She also said other factors lay ahead in determining the level of public deficits in Europe.

"There will undoubtedly still be developments in the months and weeks ahead based on the actual situation of countries and on another factor, which is obviously also determining, the scale of the recovery in growth which one can see now through some indicators," she said.
